html:
The Steilacoom are a Coast Salish people of southern Puget Sound in Washington, living near the mouth of Chambers Creek, where the town of Steilacoom now stands. They spoke Southern Lushootseed, like their neighbours the Nisqually and Puyallup.

They fished salmon, gathered shellfish and camas, and travelled the Sound by canoe. The Hudson's Bay Company built a post nearby in 1833, and the US Army set up Fort Steilacoom in 1849. In 1854 their leaders took part in the Treaty of Medicine Creek, and many members later joined neighbouring reservations. The tribe is not recognised by the US government. See also Coast Salish.
